Standardise an EDC query frame into the CTAS + ctasapp vocabulary

Standardize_Queries.Rd

Mirrors Standardize_Domain() for query records. Renames the raw query columns into the shared CTAS long-format vocabulary (subject_id, parameter_id, parameter_category_1/2, timepoint_1_name) and inner-joins the standardised subject metadata to drop queries whose subject isn't in dfSubjects. All query-specific columns are preserved unchanged so the frame stays upload-ready for the ctasapp queries table.

Usage

Standardize_Queries(dfQueries, dfSubjects, dfInput = NULL)

Arguments

dfQueries

data.frame Raw queries frame with the 15-column ctasapp contract (study, domain, field, subject_id, visit, parameter_id, query_text, query_answer, query_status, query_type, data_change, value_first_entry, value_at_query_open, value_at_query_close, value_now).

dfSubjects

data.frame Standardised subject table with studyid and subject_id.

dfInput

data.frame Optional bound CTAS input frame (typically Reporting_Input) providing the (parameter_category_2, parameter_id) mapping used to fan out queries onto the transformed CTAS parameter ids. When NULL, parameter_id is left at the raw field code.

Value

data.frame with CTAS-vocabulary key columns (subject_id, parameter_id, parameter_category_1, parameter_category_2, timepoint_1_name) and every original query column preserved.

Details

parameter_category_1 is stamped by mapping the raw domain column ("LB", "VS", "EG", "RS") onto the same human-readable labels the metric YAMLs pass to Standardize_Domain() ("Labs", "Vital Signs", "ECG", "Disease Response"). Any unrecognised domain is passed through verbatim.

When dfInput is supplied, each raw parameter_id (a field-level test code such as "AST") is fanned out into the transformed CTAS ids present in the reporting input for the same parameter_category_2 (e.g. "RANGE_AST", "MISS_AST"). This is required for the ctasapp query_table and timeseries overlay, whose joins use the transformed parameter_id. Queries whose field never appears in dfInput are dropped. site / country / studyid are not written to the output – ctasapp re-joins site onto queries from the input frame and a duplicate column would collide on dplyr::left_join(by = "subject_id").

Examples

Standardize_Queries(
  dfQueries = data.frame(
    study = "A", domain = "LB", field = "ALT",
    subject_id = "S1", visit = "WEEK 2",
    parameter_id = "ALT",
    query_text = "verify", query_answer = NA_character_,
    query_status = "Open", query_type = "Monitor",
    data_change = FALSE,
    value_first_entry = "42", value_at_query_open = "42",
    value_at_query_close = "42", value_now = "42"
  ),
  dfSubjects = data.frame(
    studyid = "A", subject_id = "S1", site = "701", country = "USA"
  )
)
#>   study domain field subject_id  visit parameter_id query_text query_answer
#> 1     A     LB   ALT         S1 WEEK 2          ALT     verify         <NA>
#>   query_status query_type data_change value_first_entry value_at_query_open
#> 1         Open    Monitor       FALSE                42                  42
#>   value_at_query_close value_now timepoint_1_name parameter_category_2
#> 1                   42        42           WEEK 2                  ALT
#>   parameter_category_1
#> 1                 Labs
